claim.why_it_matters: The single three-column 8.2.1 locale field-name table is shattered into a header line of plain text, three separate two-column tables and loose paragraphs (mon_decimal_point, mon_thousands_sep, n_cs_precedes); the Category column is lost as a column, so field-to-category association and the field/description pairing depend on reading order rather than table structure.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 99 (printed p.75) at 300 dpi. The printed 8.2.1 list is an unruled layout: a bold header line, category names (LC_MONETARY, LC_TIME) on their own lines, then indented field-name/description pairs. The markdown holds every one of these: the header, both category lines in the right places, all 12 LC_MONETARY fields (int_curr_symbol through n_cs_precedes) and both LC_TIME fields (d_fmt, t_fmt), each with its exact description, in the printed order, with every field paired with its own description on the same row or line. The only differences are presentation: the markdown alternates between pipe tables and plain indented lines, and the wrapped tail of p_cs_precedes ('a nonnegative quantity') sits on the line after the table row, exactly as it wraps in print. The printed page itself has no Category column of cells; category membership is shown by position, which the markdown keeps. No word is missing, misquoted or re-paired, so the meaning is unchanged. This is formatting/line-wrap, not a content discrepancy.
